Caroline Kennedy's paternal grandfather.why: Rarely stated, and almost only in passing: summing every phrasing searched gives at most about 50 statements (several of them copies of one Wikipedia sentence about his funeral, or news about her following him as an ambassador), against about 1,000 for each premise (P1: 'Caroline Kennedy, daughter of' 1,062; P2: "JFK's father" 722) and about 70,000 mentions of Caroline Kennedy, i.e. about 5% of either premise and under 0.1% of the subject. Searched from both ends: Joseph P. Kennedy Sr.'s Wikipedia article never names Caroline, and hers states it once, in the body, not the lead. Hence 'likely' rather than 'very_likely': it is in text, but at a twentieth of its premises (the review's Boleyn case, at 12-25%, was rated medium). Verifier re-check from Joseph P. Kennedy Sr.'s end with the 'granddaughter of' and 'Joe Kennedy' variants adds at most a few dozen hits, and the samples read are about other grandchildren (Maria Shriver), so the ratio stays around 5% and 'likely' holds.

notes: Derived edit with derived-belief and premise-route queries. Replaces the scouting's Elizabeth I / Thomas Boleyn edit, which the review rated only medium (the link is in Thomas Boleyn's Wikipedia lead and its mirrors, 12-25% of the weaker premise). Here the link was searched from both ends and is at about 5% of either premise (evidence), so 'likely'. Worlds (derived beliefs): each lists the premise that gives way and the side facts that go with it (siblings become half-siblings) and its dates; neither contradicts a firm fact about anyone outside the chain. Over-determination considered: 'Robert Kennedy was JFK's brother' plus 'Joseph P. Kennedy Sr. was Robert's father' would re-derive P2 only for full brothers, which w1 revises to half-brothers, so P2 can still give way. A world where both premises change is not minimal and is left out. The rule premise is definitional and never gives way. Curley: plausible (a Boston Irish Democrat of the same era, whose House seat JFK took in 1946; JFK's maternal grandfather, Honey Fitz, was also a Boston mayor) and clearly false. Honey Fitz himself was rejected: making him JFK's father would clash with his being Rose Kennedy's father, a firm fact outside the chain. R2 risk considered: the Kennedy surname hints at Joseph P. Kennedy Sr. in the premise questions, but no prompt contains its answer; it may make w2 likelier, which Decision 4 accepts. Near query (her mother) is neither a premise nor moved in any world. Verifier: both worlds are kept under Decision 1. They pull in many side facts (w1: Joseph Jr., Robert, Edward and the sisters become JFK's half-siblings through Rose, and P. J. Kennedy is no longer his grandfather; w2: John Jr. becomes Caroline's half-brother and Robert and Edward are no longer her uncles), but each side fact is a sibling or descent link that goes with the premise, as in the reviewer's Boleyn example and the README's Henry VII example, not a date, place or unrelated person. Read strictly ('brother' as full brother), both premises would be over-determined; this is the README's own example's weakness too. Lopsided, kept. The grandchild query's 'no' before the edit rests on her maternal grandfather, John Vernou Bouvier III, now a bridge with a check (it was unstated; formal check, FINDINGS C2).
